headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection/cascading-error if Airflow ingests prompt content from awesome-prompts, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel so overall severity stays medium.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow can make networked automation decisions, while awesome-prompts is a prompt-content repository. No shared channel is documented, but if Airflow ingests prompt text from the repo or copied snippets, instruction-like content could steer downstream tasks. Uncertainty about the bridge escalates from low to medium.
conditions: IF Airflow is configured to read prompt text from the awesome-prompts repository or copied snippets
IF any Airflow task parses that content as instructions or parameters
mitigations: Restrict Airflow DAGs to trusted, schema-validated inputs
Keep prompt repositories read-only to automation jobs
Add provenance labels before any prompt text is consumed
Review any task that turns text into commands
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow is documented with no touched data classes and awesome-prompts has no data-handling surfaces or egress. There is no evidence of shared workspace, OAuth, or sensitive data flow between them, so a leakage pathway is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF a shared workspace or secret-bearing dataset is later introduced between the two agents
mitigations: Keep the pair on separate workspaces
Do not mount secrets into either agent
Audit any future file-sharing bridge before enabling it

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, while awesome-prompts shows no write or network capability. The profiles do not show overlapping mutable resources, so direct capability conflict is limited; uncertainty stays low because no shared write surface is documented.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same filesystem, git repo, or database
mitigations: Keep write targets disjoint
Avoid giving awesome-prompts any write scope
Use separate service accounts
Add locking if a shared mutable resource is introduced

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow can operationalize outputs into scheduled workflows, and awesome-prompts is a prompt source that could be treated as authoritative text. If Airflow consumes that text without verification, errors can cascade into automated actions. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Airflow uses awesome-prompts content as an input to DAG generation or task parameters
IF no human or schema verification step exists before execution
mitigations: Insert a human review gate before execution
Validate generated parameters against a schema
Log source provenance for every imported prompt
Disable auto-deployment from text-derived artifacts
requires-engineering: separate generation from execution

E_compliance.rationale: Neither profile shows regulated data classes, residency constraints, or retention obligations. Airflow and awesome-prompts are both unverified docs-only profiles, and there is no cited compliance mismatch to assess, so no compliance risk is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data classes such as PHI, EU PII, or secrets are later routed through either agent
mitigations: Classify data before routing it
Block regulated data from unreviewed workflows
Document residency and retention settings
